title: Stable cursor adapter and error unifier for embeddings + reranker compatibility
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: Several legacy clients expect the old embeddings/rerank endpoints to return stable, replayable cursors and a narrowly defined set of HTTP error codes. New unified APIs return opaque cursors and more granular errors which breaks pagination clients and increases integration support load.

Goal: Provide a compatibility layer (adapter) that sits between the new embeddings/rerank runtime and legacy clients to: 1) translate new opaque cursors into a stable, deterministic cursor shape compatible with older SDKs; 2) map internal error variants to the legacy HTTP status and error detail contract; 3) ensure Link/next pagination semantics for streaming and non-streaming clients match legacy expectations.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change underlying model behavior, dedupe reranker results, or add new business-level retry semantics beyond preserving legacy contract.

Design summary: The adapter will canonicalize cursor payloads into a versioned wrapper: {v:2, payload:base64(kv), seq:incremental}. We will expose an opt-in header X-Compat-Version:2 for canary traffic; default behavior remains the unified API. Error mapping table will be a deterministic mapping from internal errors -> legacy codes (e.g., internal.KVMismatch -> 400 with code EMB_CURSOR_INVALID; runtime.Throttled -> 429 with retry_after; model.QualityRegression -> 424). For streaming responses the adapter will ensure a final 'cursor' event in the stream footer and preserve per-chunk offsets for partial-replay scenarios.

Trade-offs considered:
- Opaque vs structured cursor: opaque simplifies runtime but breaks debuggability; we add versioned wrapper to balance stability and opaqueness.
- Strict 1:1 error mapping may hide richer diagnostics; we include an optional X-Compat-Debug header for customers to opt in to detailed errors.
- Adapter performance: added serialization costs ~1-3ms per request in microbenchmarks; acceptable for P1 latency SLOs but requires load testing.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Legacy SDKs (v<=3.4) can paginate across embeddings/rerank endpoints without errors in compatibility mode.
- Cursor round-trip tests: generate cursor -> fetch next page -> rehydrate cursor -> yield same results (deterministic) across 95th percentile of test corpus.
- Error mapping conformance: for each canonical internal error, the adapter returns the expected legacy HTTP status and error body shape (test matrix attached).
- Streaming footer event with cursor appears in 100% of streaming sessions under compatibility mode.
- Canary rollout metrics: error-rate delta < 0.5% and p50 latency delta < 5ms at 5% traffic before wider rollout.

Migration playbook (customer-facing):
1) Enable compat mode via header or account toggle.
2) Run integration tests using our compat test harness; we provide a smoke script.
3) Validate Link header, next cursor behavior, and error mappings.
4) If issues, customers can enable X-Compat-Debug to capture detailed diagnostics and open a support ticket.

Implementation notes for ENG:
- New service x-compat/emb-rerank will be an HTTP adapter with small in-memory cursor registry for seq->kv mapping (TTL 72h). Avoid storing model outputs.
- Provide a library (python/node) to encode/decode compat cursors for SDK maintainers.
- Add unit + integration tests in eng/compat/embedding-rerank and a dedicated load test in perf/compat-cursor to validate overhead.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for cursor encode/decode, error mapping table, and header toggles.
- Integration test suite that replays 10k legacy pagination sessions across typical corpus and edge cases (empty page, last page, concurrent deletes).
- Load tests at 2x expected canary QPS to verify latency overhead.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: Feature-flagged deploy to staging + run full test harness (Week 1).
- Stage 2: Canary 5% production traffic with metrics monitored for 48h (Week 2).
- Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% after 7 days of stable metrics.
- Rollback: disable compat header or flip account toggle; run post-rollback alarm runbook.

Docs & artifacts: Confluence spec (design + mapping table), GitHub PRs, QA dashboard. Links below.
